➡️Demand for AI strong
➡️AI discovery strong
➡️Physical AI ahead

2018 created “end cycle” risk
2026 is when will “shocks pass”

To us, this is why we see less downside into year-end.

but the risk/reward for 1M, 3M and 6M positive

Big year for the railway stocks after getting left behind during the tech rally.

$UNP is a great contrast to the AI infrastructure spending boom.

Its competitive advantage is already in the ground:

Nearly 33,000 route miles connecting ports, factories, and agricultural regions across 23 states. 

Imagine trying to replicate that today. 

Buying the land. Securing rights of way. 

Building tracks, bridges, tunnels, and terminals.

The infrastructure a competitor would need to build is the infrastructure UNP already monetizes.

So naturally they are now a shareholder yield stock.

• Dividend yield: ~2%
• Trailing net buyback yield: ~2.5%
• Combined: ~4.5%

zh_summary: Applied Optoelectronics $AAOI locked in a second hyperscaler. The 2027 piece alone is about two-thirds of what the Street expects AOI to sell next year. Signed a multiyear agreement with an existing Tier-1 hyperscale datacenter customer. Mentions $ANET $COHR $FN $LITE $NVDA.
en_summary: Applied Optoelectronics $AAOI locked in a second hyperscaler. The 2027 piece alone is about two-thirds of what the Street expects AOI to sell next year. Signed a multiyear agreement with an existing Tier-1 hyperscale datacenter customer. Mentions $ANET $COHR $FN $LITE $NVDA.
text:
Applied Optoelectronics $AAOI just locked in a second hyperscaler, and the 2027 piece alone is about two-thirds of what the Street expects AOI to sell next year.

AOI signed a multiyear agreement with an existing Tier-1 hyperscale datacenter customer running from December 2026 through December 2030. The customer committed to buy about $1.5B of 800G transceivers in 2027 and about $0.7B of laser diodes in 2028 and 2029, so $2.2B in minimum commitments. For scale, AOI's total 2027 revenue is at $2.26B market consensus. AOI is covering a $2M one-time expense to speed up qualification, and the customer put in no capital.

The bigger number comes with an asterisk. "While not guaranteed, the current level of demand based on long-term discussions with the customer exceeds $10 billion over the four years of the LTA," said CFO Stefan Murry. Anything beyond the $2.2B depends on AOI bringing capacity online and winning more purchase commitments.

The detail I like most: AOI expects some of those laser diodes to power co-packaged optics starting in 2028, and it plans to expand laser manufacturing in Texas. It also committed to ship an agreed amount of product made in the USA starting in Q1 2027 and ramping through the year.

Why it matters: optics is one of the tightest parts of the AI buildout, and hyperscalers are now locking in multi-year supply the way they have for memory. AOI's problem has been capacity, with power delaying part of its US expansion and two ATM programs totaling $1.1

en_summary: $TSM is my highest-conviction holding into 2027 here's why. 1. I don't have to pick the AI winner. Nvidia's GPUs and the custom chips from Broadcom...
text:
$TSM is my highest-conviction holding into 2027 here's why.

1. I don't have to pick the AI winner.

Nvidia's GPUs and the custom chips from Broadcom, Google and Amazon are mostly built at TSMC. Every debate about GPUs versus custom silicon, or which lab ends up on top, is a debate about TSMC's customers. Share moving between them matters far less to TSMC than the total being spent. High-performance computing is now 68% of revenue.

2. The growth is accelerating at a scale that shouldn't allow it.

Q3 revenue grew 50.9% year on year. October revenue grew 59.7%. Management raised its 2026 growth forecast to about 44% in dollars, from "slightly over 40%" in July. This is a company that will do well over $150bn of revenue this year.

3. The margins tell you about the competition.

Gross margin was 66.4% and operating margin 58.7% last quarter, while absorbing the start-up cost of 2nm and of new fabs in Arizona, Japan and Germany. Press reports point to another round of wafer price increases in 2027, which TSMC has not confirmed. A company that can raise prices on Nvidia and Apple does not have a real competitor at the leading edge.

4. The next leg is already in production.

2nm went from nothing to 8% of wafer revenue in three quarters, and capacity is set to more than double in 2027. New nodes dilute margins first and add to them later. That pattern played out at 5nm and 3nm, and I expect it again.

5. It pays for its own growth.

$60-64bn of capex this year and still about $9

AMD $AMD just got its first Helios rack running inside a Microsoft Azure lab, and the stock still broke below $400.

AMD says Microsoft accepted delivery this fall, powered up its first Helios rackscale system, and reports it is successfully running early workloads in validation. Azure plans to deploy Helios at scale and is expected to be among the first clouds to put it to work on AI inference. Per Microsoft, each liquid-cooled rack packs 72 MI455X GPUs, 18 EPYC "Venice" CPUs and 31 TB of HBM4.

Why it matters: Helios is AMD's answer to Nvidia's rack scale systems, and a hyperscaler running real workloads on it is the proof point the second half ramp needs. But this is a lab, not a customer deployment. No rack counts or financial terms were shared.

The tape did not care. AMD traded as low as $396 Tuesday, its first time under $400 since May and roughly 40% below its $649.42 high on Oct. 6, as the whole AI basket gave back Monday's Nvidia rally. A Monday shelf registration is also adding to the nerves: it reportedly covers about 337 million shares for resale, including roughly 160 million each tied to the OpenAI and Meta warrants, so investors are doing dilution math on the biggest AI deals in the company's history. Registered shares are not shares sold, and AMD gets no proceeds from resale, per reports.

Beyond Warren Buffett buying shares of $TPL as a teenager in the 1940s, Murray Stahl of Horizon Kinetics discovered the company nearly five decades later.

Murray Stahl's first report for his new research service Horizon was about Texas Pacific Land $TPL and over several decades he built a position in the company that made him the largest shareholder. 

We came across Murray and TPL because he or his firm would constantly buy shares on the open market, often times just a few shares a day. 

The P symbols you see on the chart below are some of those purchases. 

I know at least two investment managers who had a chance to work directly with Murray and had nothing but nice things to say about him. 

He passed away earlier this year, the insider purchases stopped a few weeks ago and $3 billion acquisition of EagleRock Land $EROK was announced yesterday.

As I looked at the deal announcement come through, a thought crossed my mind: What would Murray think about this decision?

Hopefully we will explore the answer to that question in our next Merger Arbitrage Mondays article, unless we see a more interesting deal or a pre-deal situation come through by the end of this holiday shortened week.

Meta $META's Muse AI agent can now shop Walmart's Black Friday deals and check out for you, and it is a real test of agents with a spending limit.

Per Walmart's instructions for Muse as reported by The Verge, you tell Muse what you need, sign in to Walmart, and the first time you add an item you set up an Agent Profile with a spending limit. Then you check out inside the Muse conversation with a card saved in your Walmart account, at the same prices as http://Walmart.com. The rollout runs through Walmart's Agent Gateway and its Sparky assistant, and Walmart says Muse is just the start, with other agents on the way.

The guardrails come from Walmart's Oct. 21 announcement, which is confirmed: each agent gets its own profile, customers can require approval on every purchase or allow purchases within a limit such as $50, $100 or $200, and Walmart says agents see the same prices a human would.

Why it matters: Amazon and eBay have blocked AI agents, while Walmart is opening the door on its own terms. For Meta, Muse gets a path from chat to checkout at the biggest retailer in the country right as holiday spending peaks. For the AI compute story, every agent that books, compares and buys is inference demand that never shows up in a clickstream.

Once price clears $25.00, the next notable call gamma bars sit at $26, $28, and a larger cluster at $30.

text:
$AMD $NVDA - Now that official results are out, we see that AMD’s Venice competes very well with NVIDIA’s Vera CPU in per-thread performance in SPEC CPU 2026 intrate. 

The flagship 256-core EPYC 9996 comes close despite running at less than half the power per core, while Venice-HF is 26-38% faster than Vera thanks to 60% higher clockspeeds. 

Discounting stockfish, Venice-HF is still 21-33% faster. Even in agentic and EDA tasks which Vera excels at, Venice-HF is still 11-21% faster on a per-thread basis. --- SEMIANALYSIS
